The AI for Math fund has just announced a new grant program supporting projects that apply AI and machine learning to mathematics, with a focus on automated theorem proving, with an initial funding (from private sources) of $9.2 million.

Proposals should be aligned with one of the following categories:

  • Production grade software tools: AI for auto-formalization, proof generation, synthesis of verifiable code, and more
  • Datasets: Open-source collections of theorems, proofs, and math problems
  • Field building: Textbooks, courses, and resources to grow the AI-for-math community
  • Breakthrough ideas: High-risk, high-reward approaches to AI-driven math research

The deadline for initial expressions of interest is Jan 10, 2025.

[Disclosure: I serve on the advisory board of this fund.]

Hi all, sharing a funding opportunity that may be relevant to folks working on Lean/mathlib and AI-assisted theorem proving.

The AI for Math Fund has opened a new round of grants supporting research and open-source infrastructure at the intersection of AI and mathematics across six themes:

  • Assistance and formalization tools

  • Automation and theorem proving systems

  • Datasets and benchmarks

  • Infrastructure and integrations

  • Field-building initiatives

  • Foundational research ideas

Grants will support 12-24 months of work, with $100K-$1M awards depending on scope.

More details + application info:

  • AI for Math Fund announcement 

  • AI for Math Fund website

  • RFP details

The team will host Office Hours on Tuesday, March 17 from 11am-12pm (EST) if you have any questions (RSVP here).

Feel free to reach out if you have questions, and please share with others who might be interested.
